messages: alex: quick check — we're setting up cross-account VPC peering + an interface VPCE for partner analytics. peer CIDR 10.78.0.0/16 -> our app subnet 10.12.3.0/24. partner will initiate TLS on 443 and use ephemeral ports (30000-32767) for client-side ephemeral sockets. using SGs + NACLs. questions: 1) do we need explicit ephemeral port ranges in NACLs? 2) any mandatory log redaction rules for vpce/flow logs (partner PII concern)? 3) who signs off on the cross-account allowlist/temporary access? pinging @maria @samir for quick security ops review :eyes:
messages_2: maria: quick answers — SGs should be primary control. For our app: inbound SG allow TCP 443 from 10.78.0.0/16. Outbound SG allow ephemeral range back to 10.78.0.0/16 if app initiates responses. NACLs are stateless so keep them broad and let SGs do fine-grained work. For flow logs: redact request headers/URI that might contain PII; keep src/dst/port, action, bytes. We mask X-User-* and Authorization headers at ingestion. Ops approval: @ops-jen to sign off. :white_check_mark:
messages_3: samir: nit — ephemeral ports from partner are source ports on their side; our SG inbound should accept TCP 443 dest port. Responses will use ephemeral dest ports on their side so outbound rules should allow high ports as dest. For NACLs, allow TCP 443 in/out for the peer CIDR and a permissive ephemeral high port range (1024-65535) if you want to avoid dropped packets. Also update VPCE endpoint policy to restrict to only the S3/specific APIs the partner needs. Send allowlist request to partnerships@redwood with CIDR + expiry window. :+1:
messages_4: ops-jen: I can do the sign-off. please create a minimal infra PR and attach the runbook snippet + expected change window. I'll need the JIRA ticket and the exact CIDR + account id. Also confirm retention window for flow logs after redaction. If it's temporary access, we'll set a 7-day TTL by default unless legal asks otherwise.
messages_5:
alex: adding infra snippet now. example NACL/SG quick draft below — will put full config in PR.

```
# Security Group (app-for-partner)
Inbound: 443 TCP from 10.78.0.0/16
Outbound: 1024-65535 TCP to 10.78.0.0/16

# NACL (subnet-level, stateless)
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 443 10.78.0.0/16
Rule 110: ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 10.78.0.0/16
Rule * : DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0
```

Will open PR with that and the runbook. tagging partnerships + infra change window: Friday midnight UTC?
messages_6: maria: small tweak — don't restrict NACLs to 30000-32767 specifically; keep the broader ephemeral range 1024-65535 to avoid odd drops. Also add a flow-log transform that strips query strings and X-User-* headers before storage. Example transform rule: `mask_headers: ["Authorization", "X-User-Email", "X-User-Id"]`. We'll verify with privacy before retention is final.
messages_7: samir: also ensure source/dest check remains enabled on any EC2 that acts as a bridge. For VPCE peering, confirm route table entries only point to the exact peer CIDRs (no 0.0.0.0/0 leaks). I'll run a quick config lint once PR is up.
messages_8: security-bot: automated note — created ticket INF-2345 for cross-account vpce allowlist review. Please reference INF-2345 in the PR. No blocking findings from quick static checks. :robot_face:
messages_9: alex: thanks all — i'll file PR + attach runbook + INF-2345. ops-jen, will request sign-off once PR is ready. closing thread after sign-off. :pray:
